legs.title: Santa Monica
legs.description: We stayed in a hostel near Santa Monica Pier. We weren't prepared for how cool the palm trees that lined all the streets would be.

legs.title: Hollywood
legs.description: We stayed in a hotel in Hollywood within walking distance of the Chinese Theater, where we saw The Odyssey. We also walked to Yamashiro - "Mountain Castle" - and the Hollywood Bowl. Also in our days in LA: Grand Central Market, The Last Bookstore, Little Tokyo, Motion Picture Museum, Griffith Observatory, Getty Museum,  Beverly Hills, Greystone Mansion and Laurel Canyon.

legs.title: Pasadena / Gamble House
legs.description: We had a tour of Gamble House, designed by Greene and Greene in 1908.

legs.title: Las Vegas
legs.description: We aren't into the Las Vegas sins - except maybe neon - but the Pinball Hall of Fame was great. Maybe 200 working pinball machines dating from the 50s. Plus we went to cirque du soleil, and ate at a Las Vegas buffet, which I hear might be going away.

legs.title: Hoover Dam
legs.description: Hoover Dam was closed for security reasons that nobody would explain. We just got photos of a donkey in the middle of the road.

legs.title: Grand Canyon
legs.description: Did a small part of the Bright Angel trial. It very was hot. Would like to do a multi-day hike to the river someday.

legs.title: Horseshoe Bend
legs.description: This is the Colorado river in Page, Colorado on the road between the Grand Canyon and Zion. Needed to walk in 110 degree weather, but not too bad for the great view.

legs.title: Bryce Canyon
legs.description: Probably the most memorable hikes of the trip. Would of been better if we came in the Fall though.

legs.title: Death Valley
legs.description: Not much to see here, but we got a nice picture in front of the sign - 120F / 49C!

legs.title: Manzanar - Japanese Internment Camp
legs.description: The camp's buildings are not there any more, but you can drive around the camp and see the foundations to get a sense of the scope of the place. Also a very good museum. There will be similar museums about today's internment camps.

legs.title: Yosemite
legs.description: Yosemite is crowded for good reason, so we weren't there long. Traffic! But we did a good hike to Lembert Dome - not Half Dome or El Capitan, but a good challenge for us, and a great view.

legs.title: Monterey
legs.description: Monterey Aquarium and Carmel. Also the famous "17 Mile Drive" which turned out to be the ocean views along Pebble Beach golf course. Oregon coast was better.

legs.title: San Francisco
legs.description: We stayed for three days in the "Royal Pacific Motor Inn" which is between Chinatown and Little Italy and around the corner from City Lights bookstore. Also easy to walk to Coit Tower and the Embarcadero.  We needed to drive and Uber to Golden Gate bridge and Little Japan. Also spent a day in Silicon Valley - Apple, Google and the Computer History Museum. Golden Gate bridge was a highlight.

legs.title: Charles Shultz Museum
legs.description: Awesome museum for Peanuts fans in Santa Rosa, where Shultz did most of his work. Bottom floor is devoted to the comics, and upper floor to Shultz's life, including his actual studio. Worthy of Shultz; everything a Peanuts fan could want.

legs.title: Pacific Coast Highway / Redwoods
legs.description: Many options for hikes in different redwood groves, and you mostly have them to yourself. Not too hot in early August. The stops and hikes on the Oregon coast are unbelievable, and you have them all to yourself.  Could easily spend a week on those.

legs.title: Eureka & Tillamook
legs.description: The Oregon coast was a surprise - 101 goes along long stretches of publicly owned shore, not much "beach" but lots of cliffs leading down to the water. We could have spent a week in something called "Samuel H. Boardman State Scenic Corridor" - lots of hikes in the redwoods and along the shore. We stayed in Eureka (which became rich around 1900 but is now pretty rough) and went to the cheese factory in Tillamook.

legs.title: Seattle
legs.description: We met Paul in Seattle and he showed us his building and the Amazon spheres. Stayed at the Mediterranean Inn which was a short walk from Paul's apartment and around the corner from KEXP and the Mecca restaurant - nice place and worth it. Hotel had bikes so we took a ride near the water.

legs.title: Will at College
legs.description: We got back and two days later Will started college.
